 Oral Judgment

(PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIKHIL S. KARIEL)
1.

By way of this appeal under Section 378(1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'CRPC'), the appellant-State, seeks to assail the judgment and order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Patan in Sessions Case No.517 of 2002 dated 04.02.2005, more particularly, whereby the learned Sessions Court has acquitted the sole accused for the offences punishable under Sections 366 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1273/2005 JUDGMENT DATED: 04/10/2025 undefined 2.

The case of the prosecution, in brief, being that the prosecutrix, i.e., the daughter of the original complainant, had been abducted by the accused on 21.06.1999 and whereas, the accused and the prosecutrix had been apprehended on 25.02.2002.

The case of the prosecution being that the accused having abducted the prosecutrix, had threatened her with dire consequences and had confined her during the period in question and had physically assaulted and had raped the prosecutrix repeatedly.

It would appear that the investigating officer had laid the charge-sheet and whereas, the charges were framed by the learned Sessions Court on 29.12.2004, whereafter the trial had been conducted and the learned Sessions Court concerned, as noted herein above, had recorded the finding of acquittal in favour of the accused, being aggrieved by which, the State has preferred this appeal.

3. Heard learned APP Ms. Jirga Jhaveri, who would submit that there was sufficient evidence on record to show that the accused had forcefully abducted the prosecutrix and whereas, he had committed the offences punishable under Section 376 of the IPC and whereas, the learned Sessions Court, without appreciating the evidence on record, had acquitted the opponent-accused and whereas, the learned APP would submit that this Court may interfere with the said finding and may convict the accused for the offences, as alleged.

4. Having heard the learned APP and having perused the documents on record, at the outset, before examining the same, we would rely upon the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Babu Sahebagouda Rudragoudar & NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1273/2005 JUDGMENT DATED: 04/10/2025 undefined Ors. vs. State of Karnataka, reported in (2024) 8 SCC Page 149.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the aforequoted paragraph, has laid down the parameters, which are to be considered by an Appellate Court while considering an appeal, where the trial court has recorded a finding of acquittal in favour of the accused.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has, inter alia

,
laid down that the Appellate Court has to come to a conclusion either that the judgment of acquittal suffers from a patent perversity, or that the same is based on misreading or omission of material evidence on record, or that there is only one view possible, which is consistent with the guilt of the accused, more particularly, upon examining the evidence on record.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has further laid down that the Appellate Court, has to give specific reasons while overturning a finding of acquittal in favour of the accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1273/2005 JUDGMENT DATED: 04/10/2025 undefined 6.

Considering the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court from the perspective of the fact situation, we are of the considered opinion that the present is neither a case of the impugned judgment suffering from any patent perversity, nor we are of the opinion that the learned Sessions Court has misread or omitted to appreciate the material evidence or that there was only one view possible, which was consistent with the guilt of the accused.

7. To this Court, it would appear that the present is a clear case of a major lady, having eloped with a person of her choice and whereas, only on account of an FIR having been registered by the mother of the prosecutrix at the relevant point of time, the entire rigmarole had to be followed.

From the evidence, we notice the fact that while the allegation is that the accused had forcibly abducted or forced the prosecutrix to go along with him, yet on the date when the prosecutrix was abducted by the accused, they had met a witness, who had been later declared as hostile, yet, who in his deposition, has said that he had met the accused and the prosecutrix and whereas, the learned Sessions Court has noted that there was no attempt on the part of the prosecutrix to complain to the said person that she was being forcibly abducted.
Rather it appears, that the prosecutrix was a willing accomplice and not a forcible partner.

It would also appear in this regard that while the FIR had been registered on 21.06.1999, the accused and the prosecutrix were apprehended on 25.02.2002, i.e., after approximately two and half years and whereas, during the interregnum, there is no evidence to suggest that the prosecutrix had ever NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1273/2005 JUDGMENT DATED: 04/10/2025 undefined attempted to escape from the clutches of the accused,
if it was a case of forcible abduction, more particularly, when the evidence goes to suggest that the prosecutrix had multiple opportunities to do the same. It would appear in this regard that the accused and the prosecutrix, had first gone to Patan, and from there, they had gone in a luxury bus to a place called Mandali, where they had sought for work at a factory, and having not got any work,
the accused and the prosecutrix had traveled to Rajasthan in a truck and whereas, they had rented a room at Rajasthan and whereas, the accused started doing masonry work at such place.

It comes out very clearly from the evidence that, at no point of time, when the accused and the prosecutrix were State Of Gujarat vs Rajput Popatji Bhuraji on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20086713/
3 residing together at Rajasthan, more particularly, in presence of neighbours, that the prosecutrix had ever complained about the accused having forcibly abducted her.

sentences.text: Moreover, though the present was a case where the allegation was for an offence under Section 376 of the IPC, yet, it appears that there was no medical examination of either the prosecutrix or the accused, clearly leading to a conclusion that the present was a clear case of no evidence.

8. Considering the material on record and the examination of the material by the learned Sessions Court, we are of the firm opinion that the prosecution could not bring home the charge of the accused having either abducted the prosecutrix or having raped the prosecutrix against her will.

We are of the opinion that the impugned decision is not a case of patent perversity and whereas, we are also of the opinion that the learned Sessions Court has neither misread the evidence nor NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1273/2005 JUDGMENT DATED: 04/10/2025 undefined has omitted any crucial piece of evidence.
We are also of the considered opinion that in the present case, there was no possibility of two views, and rather, the only view which was possible, was not consistent with the guilt of the accused.

9. At this stage, we are also conscious of the fact that the alleged incident had taken place in the year 1999 whereas the prosecutrix and the accused were apprehended in the month of February, 2002 and whereas, the learned Sessions Court had passed the impugned decision on 04.02.2005, that is to say, that all the events had taken place approximately more than two decades ago.

To this Court,
while we are of the opinion that there is no reason whatsoever for us to interfere with the impugned decision, even otherwise, considering the fact that more than two decades have elapsed, we would have been otherwise very circumspect in interfering with such a decision.
10. For the reasons above, the present appeal fails and is disposed of as rejected.

Record &
Proceedings, if any, be sent back to the trial court forthwith.
